question: Which patients require standard precautions?
explanation: Standard precautions protect healthcare workers from unknown infections in any patient, so they apply to everyone. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the main goal of using standard precautions in a clinic?

options.B: Lowering the cost of hospital consumables
options.D: Eliminating the need for isolation rooms

explanation: These measures stop infections from spreading between patients and staff. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: When must you use soap and water for hand hygiene instead of alcohol rubs?

options.A: Immediately after taking a patient's pulse
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt
options.C: Every hour during a routine morning shift
options.D: Before entering a sterile operating theatre

explanation: Soap and water physically remove visible dirt and certain spores that alcohol cannot kill. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why do nurses prefer alcohol-based rubs for routine hand hygiene between patients?

options.A: They destroy most microbes quickly and save time
options.B: They completely sterilize the skin surface permanently
options.C: They replace the need for wearing medical gloves
options.D: They leave a protective chemical film on the hands

explanation: Alcohol rubs work fast against many germs and are easy to use at the bedside. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is the main reason to wear a medical gown during client care?

options.A: To replace the requirement for hand hygiene
options.B: To keep the healthcare worker warm in cold wards
options.C: To prevent soiling of clothing and skin exposure
options.D: To identify senior nursing staff on the unit

explanation: Gowns block splashes and sprays from reaching your uniform or skin. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: A nurse is assisting with a wound irrigation that might spray fluid. What PPE is essential?

options.A: A sterile gown and double shoe covers
options.B: Gloves, mask, and protective eye wear
options.C: A clean surgical cap and rubber boots
options.D: Heavy utility gloves and a hair net

explanation: Procedures with splash risks require protection for your hands, face, eyes, and mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the safest way to handle a needle right after giving an injection?

options.A: Drop it straight into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.B: Recap it firmly using both hands before disposal
options.C: Break the needle tip off to save bin space
options.D: Place it gently on the nearest medication tray

explanation: Putting sharps straight into a rigid container prevents accidental needle sticks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why is two-handed needle recapping strongly discouraged?

options.A: It dulls the sharp tip making future use difficult
options.B: It causes the syringe barrel to crack and leak medicine
options.C: It greatly increases the risk of accidental finger pricks
options.D: It violates standard drug preparation protocols

explanation: Holding the cap with one hand while guiding a needle often leads to missing the cap and stabbing your other hand. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which action is a key part of respiratory hygiene when you need to cough?

options.A: Wiping hands on a shared lab coat
options.B: Sneezing directly into open bare palms
options.C: Turning the head toward nearby patients
options.D: Covering the mouth and nose with a tissue

explanation: Tissues trap respiratory droplets so they do not spread into the air or onto surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: What should you do when a patient arrives at the clinic with a persistent cough?

options.A: Ignore the symptom if the patient has normal vitals
options.B: Insist they wait outside the compound gates completely
options.C: Provide a surgical mask and direct them to a spaced area

explanation: Masks and physical distance help stop airborne droplets from reaching other patients. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which hospital surfaces need the most frequent cleaning?

options.A: Interior walls far away from patient beds
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and handles
options.D: Ceiling boards and upper window frames

explanation: Frequently touched areas collect germs fast and easily spread them to others. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: How should a nurse manage a reusable tool like a stethoscope after use?

options.A: Wipe it with a dry tissue only if it looks dusty
options.B: Clean and disinfect it before using on another patient
options.C: Store it in the pocket until the end of the shift
options.D: Soak it overnight in plain tap water in the utility room

explanation: Disinfecting shared tools stops them from carrying germs between clients. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the first step to take after a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound hard to force out trapped blood
options.B: Wash the exposed area thoroughly with soap and water
options.C: Apply strong antiseptic spirit directly onto the puncture
options.D: Complete an official hospital incident report form

explanation: Washing the site immediately lowers the amount of germs or virus entering the wound. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why must a needle-stick injury be reported quickly?

options.A: To ensure the nurse gets excused from work for a week
options.B: To allow timely assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis
options.C: To prevent the ward manager from issuing a query
options.D: To replace the broken instrument with a new brand

explanation: Post-exposure medications work best when started within hours of an exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)
